title: Closures in practical UI examples
learningObjectives: Explain closures in practical ui examples and reason about JavaScript execution and function behaviour.

understand.concept: A closure is created when a function retains access to variables from its lexical environment after the outer function has finished executing. Closures are commonly used for private state, event handlers, and function factories.
understand.whyItMatters: Closures allow UI handlers to remember configuration or state without using global variables. They can also retain large objects unintentionally, so lifecycle cleanup matters.
understand.analogy: A closure is like a function carrying a small backpack of the variables it needs from where it was created.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript scope, execution, identity, and scheduling follow language and engine semantics.

explain.narrative: The returned function retains access to count even though makeCounter has returned.

examples.explanation: The returned function retains access to count even though makeCounter has returned.
examples.expectedOutput: Console output demonstrates the language behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Create a button handler with a closure-based counter. Add a reset action and explain which variables remain private to the closure.
practise.independentTask: Create a small example that demonstrates the concept, test edge cases, and explain the execution or reference behaviour in your own words.
hints: Track variable scope and object references carefully.
Predict output before running the code.
Include cleanup and a stopping condition where required.
